key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval, a frozen foundation-model prior, and shift-aware correction to stay accurate across changing weather and day-night regimes.
engineering_relevance: The method supports more reliable PV dispatch and grid integration by better handling rare but operationally critical conditions such as ramps, peaks, and nighttime transitions.
method: Retrieves historical patches and analog trajectories matched on temporal shape, power level, PV state, and intra-day period.
Calibrates the retrieved forecast with a frozen Chronos foundation model via a lightweight residual adapter.
Applies physics-aware distribution-shift correction and a regime-weighted loss for peak, ramping, night-time, and regular samples.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a PV forecasting framework evaluated through its ability to correct regime-dependent errors under weather and diurnal distribution shifts, but it does not report specific metrics here.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of historical retrieval and the reliability of the hand-crafted regime/shift features used for correction.
paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
